reason: Core test (log2 kissat/cms conflicts vs k for planted SAT and random UNSAT, c<=0.6 vs c>=1) is discriminating in principle: 2^{0.6k} vs 2^{1.5k} differ ~20x by k=8-12. But as written it is not runnable and has confounds. (1) Budget: pilot (pilot_gen.py, S_3 bit-circuit with explicit quotient, kissat --conflicts) measured ~2.5k conflicts/s; k=6,L=18: SAT 6.5-11k conflicts 2-4 s, UNSAT 22-24k conflicts 9-12 s; k=8,L=24 SAT 23k conflicts 15 s, UNSAT over 60 s. Grid 3p x 7k x 100 inst x 2 arms = 4200 runs is hours, UNSAT k>=8 cells hit the 60 s cap -> right-censored fit; 18 CPU-min covers ~100-150 runs. (2) Wall-time cap makes censoring non-deterministic; cap must be a conflict cap. (3) Grid decouples k and log p: expected spurious solutions 2^{2k}/p varies from 16 (k=12,p=2^20) to 2^-4, mixing satisfiable-by-luck regime with unique-planted regime; c is confounded with solution density. (4) 'x1 free' control is not a null: S_3 is quadratic in x1, almost every x2 gives a root, so instances are trivially SAT, no UNSAT arm, and it does not test whether c comes from Semaev structure vs generic modular-multiplier hardness. (5) k=6..12 spans only 6 doublings; conflict floor ~3k at k=4 (log p-bit arithmetic) biases fitted c downward for SAT; need curvature check. (6) Independence-of-log-p claim is untested by the grid because k/log p co-varies. Pilot early read (not the experiment, tiny n): UNSAT slope ~1.6 per k (k=4:~2.5k, k=6:~23k conflicts), SAT slope ~0.4-0.6 but noisy; consistent with prior c>=1 for the proof-bearing arm. Extrapolation to n=131 is only one-sided: c>=1 on UNSAT at k up to ~9 closes resolution-based solvers on this encoding in the toy range; c<0.6 would only license a larger-k run, not a claim at k=43. No bearing on any deployed curve.
fix: Redesign. (A) Ray: couple log p = 3k (also a second ray log p = 4k) so expected spurious solutions are 2^-k as at n=131; k in {4,5,6,7,8,9}; fixed-k cut: k=6, log p in {18,24,30,36} to test independence of log p. (B) Instances per cell: 8 planted (P1,P2 curve points with x<2^k, xR=x(P1+P2)) + 8 random xR; label every instance by brute force (enumerate x1<2^k, solve quadratic with PARI/sympy sqrt_mod) and assert planted SAT / count solutions; also assert CNF model count equals brute force at k<=5 (encoding correctness gate). (C) Metric: kissat 'conflicts' (and cryptominisat5 conflicts, one XOR/Gauss-on run with --xor/--maxxorsize as the idea's XOR arm) with a hard CONFLICT cap 2^18 (kissat --conflicts=, cms --maxconfl); never wall time; report censored fraction; fit log2 median conflicts vs k only on cells with >=75% completions, use Tobit/Kaplan-Meier or report lower bound c_min treating capped as cap; bootstrap CI over instances; fit on k in {4..6} and {7..9} separately to expose curvature; SAT and UNSAT separately. (D) Null arms replacing 'x1 free': (i) matched-random-polynomial control: same circuit with random bivariate G(x1,x2)=sum r_ij x1^i x2^j (i,j<=2) mod p, same size/degree, planted root, to separate Semaev structure from modular-arithmetic hardness; (ii) enumeration baseline counted in the same sweep: 2^k sqrt-mod calls (units: modular square roots) and hybrid Coppersmith+guess count as the explicit 2^k comparator; (iii) shuffled-target UNSAT control where xR is replaced by a random residue with matched bit pattern. (E) Success rule: route alive only if UNSAT and SAT both c<=0.6 with CI upper <0.9 and null (D.i) shows c>=1; closed for resolution solvers if UNSAT c_lower>=1. (F) Budget: ~6 k x 2 arms(+null) x 16 inst x mean 6 s; cap per-run at conflict 2^18 and CPU total 18 min; run kissat and cms in parallel processes and report CPU not wall. Mark a larger-k (k up to 14, log p=42) run as follow-up only if c<0.8.

pilot.note: k=8 remaining instances exceeded 120 s tool limit and were killed. Planted=SAT and random=UNSAT status checks passed in all completed rows (k=5,L=15 also 3+3). n=3 per cell, not evidence for c.
